TO:  JOSEPH M. HOEFGEN, CITY MANAGER

FROM:  JUDY SMITH, ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER

SUBJECT:  MONTHLY FINANCIAL REPORT - SEPTEMBER 2010

Status Report

What is the status of the City’s budget at the end of the first quarter of fiscal year 2010-11?

We are still in the early stages of the fiscal year and both the revenue and expenditure activity is
consistent with historical year to date. Club concession (+13%) and development fees (+2%) are
running better than expected, but may also reflect seasonal variation for these items. All other
revenues are less than expected with total general fund revenue at -3% and all revenues, including
restricted special revenue, at 18% less than expected. These numbers will improve as we move
through the balance of the year.

Total operating expenditures are currently 4% less than expected for year to date, and all
departments, except insurance/attorney are below expected. The reason the insurance/attorney
expenditures are higher is solely due to insurance activity, as the City Attorney’s costs reflect only
one month’s billing. All insurance premium deposits for CJPIA programs (general liability,
workers compensation, property and pollution liability) are due July 1st of the fiscal year. As
operating departments are “charged” for the cost of insurance throughout the year through our
monthly allocation, revenue from the charges flows back to the insurance fund and offsets the initial
cost. In addition, the City staff took advantage of a one-time, pre-payment option from the CJPIA
and realized a $10,000 savings (6%) on the outstanding retro-deposit that was due, as the Authority
moved from the retro-deposit process to prefunding of the liability and workers compensation
programs. We will be bringing a budget adjustment to Council at fiscal year-end to reflect this
discounted payment.

Spot Reports

None

TO:  JOSEPH HOEFGEN, CITY MANAGER

FROM:  JUDY SMITH, ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER

SUBJECT:  ESTABLISH A FEE FOR CANDIDATE STATEMENTS CONSISTENT
  WITH THE REQUIREMENTS OF RESOLUTION NO. R96-47

The Issue

Shall the City Council confirm the provisions of Resolution R96-47 regarding foreign language
translation and printing of Candidate Statements and establish a fee for the Candidate Statements
consistent with the resolution?

Background and Analysis

1.  Section 13307 of the Election Code of the State of California provides that each candidate
  for local elective office may prepare a candidate’s statement on a form provided by the City
  Clerk.

2.  Candidate statements are optional, but must be filed at the same time nomination papers
  are filed with the City Clerk. The candidate statement is printed in the sample ballot
  mailed to all registered voters.

3.  The City Clerk may estimate the cost of printing the candidate statement and establish a
  required deposit to be paid at the time nomination papers are filed.

If a candidate files a candidate statement, that statement is printed in English in the sample ballot
that is mailed to all voters. In accordance with state law, a candidate may request that the statement
be translated and printed in Spanish. In addition, as a result of the Federal Voting Rights Act of
1992 and due to the composition of the resident population, candidate statements are required to be
translated and printed in Chinese. We have fulfilled this foreign language requirement by: 1.)
Providing a statement on the sample ballot that a Chinese translation is available and will be mailed
to any voter upon request by contacting City Hall; 2.) Duplicating and mailing to each voter who
has indicated to the County Registrar that they wish to receive a Chinese language voting materials
(22 mailed in 2009) and, 3.) Providing a copy of the Chinese language materials (voter pamphlet
and ballot) for review at each precinct on election day.

Since the implementation of foreign language translation requirements, the City Council determined
that candidates should not bear the cost of the federally mandated Chinese translation and printing.
During the 2009 election, the cost for the candidate information in the Chinese sample ballot (which
was photocopied and distributed upon request) totaled ~$1,350. The City’s position in the past, and
as contained in Resolution R96-47, is to require candidates to pay for the Spanish translation
CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
OCTOBER 12, 2010
  9
 (~$200), since this is performed at the candidate’s option, but not for the cost of the printing. No
candidate during the tenure of the current City Clerk has requested a Spanish translation.

The deposit in 2009 for printing of the candidate statement in English was set at $275 staff is
recommending a deposit of $275 for 2011. If the cost exceeds this amount, the City Clerk may bill
the candidates a pro-rata share. If the cost is less, a refund can be issued.

Fiscal Impact

The City has budgeted a total of $28,800 for the 2011 election services, which assumes the city
would bear the cost of the Chinese translation and all foreign language printing. A revenue offset
for candidate statement fees in the amount of $1,350 is included in the FY 10-11 budget.

Alternatives Available to the City Council

1.  Revise the City’s policy with respect to foreign translations and printing as required by the
  federal voting rights act and require candidates to bear these costs and direct staff to prepare
  a new resolution and deposit fee.

2.  Confirm Resolution R96-47 regarding foreign translations and costs associated with
  candidate statements. Staff recommends a deposit fee of $275, which would cover the
  anticipated cost of printing the candidate statements in English in the sample ballot. If a
  candidate wishes their statement translated and printed in Spanish, the City Clerk will bill
  the candidate directly based on actual cost for the Spanish translation.

Recommendation

It is recommended that the City Council confirm Resolution R96-47 and establish the candidate
statement deposit fee in the amount of $275 for the March 8, 2011 General Municipal Election.

TO:  MAYOR HUMPHREY AND HONORABLE CITY COUNCILMEMBERS

FROM:  CHRISTI HOGIN, CITY ATTORNEY

SUBJECT:  Easement agreement with the South Bay Cities Sanitation District of Los Angeles
  County granting a non-exclusive easement for purposes of constructing and
  maintaining a retaining wall within the Paseo Lunado Canyon east of the intersection
  of Via Carrillo and Paseo Lunado to protect against slope failure and potential
  damage to the District’s trunk sewer line that traverses the area.

The Issue

Whether to enter into an easement agreement with the South Bay Cities Sanitation District of Los
Angeles County granting a non-exclusive easement for purposes of constructing and maintaining a
retaining wall within the Paseo Lunado Canyon east of the intersection of Via Carrillo and Paseo
Lunado to protect against slope failure and potential damage to the District’s trunk sewer line that
traverses the area.

Fiscal Impact: None.

Analysis and Discussion

The South Bay Cities Sanitation District of Los Angeles County is a public entity that owns and
maintains large-diameter trunk sewers throughout Los Angeles County, including a trunk sewer line
within the Paseo Lunado Canyon east of the intersection of Via Carrillo and Paseo Lunado. In or
around February 2010, a portion of the slope in Paseo Lunado Canyon above the trunk sewer failed
and caused the trunk sewer to break, leading to a sewage spill. The slope failure also damaged a
pedestrian access path. The slope failure prevents ready pedestrian access to the area and continues
to pose a threat of additional damage to the trunk sewer. The District proposes to construct a
retaining wall in the area to guard against additional slope failures and to protect its sewer line.
On May 18, 2010, the Planning Commission approved the construction of the retaining wall subject
to the condition that the District enter into a license agreement with the City to authorize access to
the City property necessary for the construction and maintenance of the wall. After discussion
between the District’s counsel and the City Attorney’s Office, it was determined that an easement
agreement would be the most appropriate instrument. The non-exclusive easement agreement
attached provides the District with the property rights necessary to construct and maintain the
retaining wall on City-owned property. This agreement is the functional equivalent of a license
agreement and satisfies the condition imposed by the Planning Commission. Should the trunk
sewer line ever be abandoned by the District or otherwise taken out of service, the easement granted
by the agreement will automatically extinguish. The easement agreement also requires the District
to maintain liability insurance and to indemnify the City for any claims that may arise as a result of
the District’s construction, maintenance or repair of the wall.
CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
OCTOBER 12, 2010
  11
 Recommendation

Adopt Resolution No. 10-24 approving and easement agreement with the South Bay Cities
Sanitation District of Los Angeles County granting a non-exclusive easement for purposes of
constructing and maintaining a retaining wall within the Paseo Lunado Canyon east of the
intersection of Via Carrillo and Paseo Lunado to protect against slope failure and potential damage
to the District’s trunk sewer line that traverses the area and authorize Mayor to execute the
agreement on behalf of the City.

SUBJECT:  SPECIAL EVENT APPLICATION FOR THE COMPASSIONATE FRIENDS
  ORGANIZATION TO HOLD A LOCAL EVENT OF THE WORLDWIDE
  CHILDREN’S MEMORIAL CANDLE LIGHTING AT THE FOUNTAIN IN
  MALAGA COVE PLAZA

DATE:  OCTOBER 12, 2010

ISSUE

Shall a Special Event Application be approved for the Compassionate Friends organization to hold a
local event of the Worldwide Children’s Memorial Candle Lighting on Sunday, December 12, 2010
from 6:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. at Neptune Fountain in Malaga Cove Plaza?

BACKGROUND AND ANALYSIS

Compassionate Friends is a worldwide organization with a local chapter meeting in Palos Verdes
Estates for approximately 17 years. The organization assists and supports families that have had their
child pass away at any age or of any cause. Every year, on the second Sunday of December, the
Compassionate Friends sponsors a Worldwide Candle Lighting to honor and remember those children
of families that have died.

This is the third year that sponsors have requested the event be held within City limits. Since the event
has been held successfully and without incident in the past, sponsors are requesting the event be held
again in Palos Verdes Estates. The event will have music, an inspirational message and the reading of
local children’s names that are being remembered. It is expected that there will be between 150-250
people in attendance.

Event sponsors have secured a comprehensive Special Event Application. The Application has been
reviewed and preliminarily approved by all municipal departments. All fees have been paid and the
Indemnity Agreement have been received. An updated Certificate of Insurance will be received prior
to the event. Notice will be provided to business owners that may be affected.

Event organizers are aware of the necessity to have a safe event with a proper clean-up afterward.

 RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the City Council approve the Special Event Application for Compassionate
Friends to hold their local event of the Worldwide Children’s Memorial Candle Lighting on
December 12, 2010 from 6:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. at Neptune Fountain in Malaga Cove Plaza.

TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL

FROM:  JOSEPH M. HOEFGEN, CITY MANAGER

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION SUPPORTING PROPOSITION 22 – THE LOCAL
  TAXPAYER, PUBLIC SAFETY AND TRANSPORTATION ACT OF
  2010

The Issue

Shall the City Council approve a Resolution Supporting Proposition 22 – The Local Taxpayer
Public Safety and Transportation Act of 2010?

Background and Analysis

Council will recall that in November 2004, California voters overwhelmingly passed Proposition
1A with 84% of votes cast in support of this measure. Proposition 1A was intended to protect
revenues collected by cities, counties, and special districts from being transferred to the State of
California for statewide use. The measure included a provision (beginning in 2006) enabling the
State to suspend the protections of Proposition 1A if the Governor declares a fiscal necessity and
two-thirds of the California State Legislature approves the suspension. While the State
subsequently exercised the option to “borrow” local government property taxes funds per the
provisions of Proposition 1A, local government revenues continue to be at risk.

Over the years, California voters have passed separate ballot measures to dedicate local funding
sources to essential local services and to prevent the State from shifting or raiding local
government, transit and transportation funds. Despite the safeguards of Proposition 1A and other
measures, in 2009-10, the State passed a budget that borrowed and redirected approximately $5
billion in city, county, transit, redevelopment and special district funds on a statewide basis.

Based on the repeated “takes” of local government revenue by the State of California, there is cause
for significant concern that the State will take billions more in local government funding in future
years unless additional safeguards are implemented. In Palos Verdes Estates, the largest single
threat to our city’s financial stability has been adverse action by the State of California. Without
question, the State’s continuing efforts to borrow and redirect traditional local government funding
has jeopardized local government services on a statewide basis.

Based on these continuing concerns, a broad coalition has been developed by the League of
California Cities to qualify Proposition 22 for the November 2, 2010 statewide ballot. As described
in more detail in the attached background materials, Proposition 22, the Local Taxpayer, Public
Safety and Transportation Protection Act, would:
CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
OCTOBER 12, 2010
  15
   •  Prohibit the State from taking, borrowing or redirecting local taxpayer funds dedicated to
  public safety, emergency response and other vital local government services. Prop 22 would
  close loopholes to prevent taking local taxpayer funds currently dedicated to cities, counties,
  and special districts. It would also revoke the State’s authority to borrow local government
  property tax funds.

  •  Protect vital, dedicated transportation and public transit funds from State raids. Prop 22
  would prohibit the State from redirecting, borrowing or taking the gasoline excise tax
  (HUTA) allocated to cities and counties for local street and road maintenance and
  improvements. Prop 22 also prohibits the State from taking or redirecting public
  transportation account revenues dedicated to public transit.

  •  Protect local taxpayers by keeping more of our local tax dollars local where there’s more
  accountability to voters, and by ensuring once and for all that our gas taxes go to fund road
  improvements. Prop 22 also reduces pressure for local tax and fee increases that become
  necessary when the State redirects local funds.

While a State budget is in the final states of adoption at the writing of this staff report, the State
budget appears to rely on the receipt of billions of dollars in federal assistance which is far from
certain. As a result, the State budget will remain only very tenuously balanced, and there is little
doubt that the $19 billion dollar deficit that has loomed over the State budget will resurface shortly.

Based on the past practice of the State to redirect local government funding, staff has prepared the
attached Resolution supporting the passage of Proposition 22 for Council review and recommended
adoption. A listing of the 288 cities that have taken a position of support for the passage of
Proposition 22 is the final attachment to this report.

Alternatives Available to City Council

  1. Adopt Resolution R10-23 supporting Proposition 22 – The Local Taxpayer, Public Safety
  and Transportation Act of 2010 on the November 2, 2010 California General Election ballot.

  2. Adopt Resolution R10-23 supporting Proposition 22 – The Local Taxpayer, Public Safety
  and Transportation Act of 2010 on the November 2, 2010 California General Election ballot
  with modifications

  3. Decline to Act

Recommendation

It is recommended that the City Council adopt Resolution R10-23 supporting Proposition 22 – The
Local Taxpayer, Public Safety and Transportation Act of 2010 on the November 2, 2010 California
General Election ballot.

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION R10-20; CALLING FOR THE ELECTION OF CERTAIN CITY
  OFFICERS AND RESOLUTION R10-21; REQUESTING THE COUNTY
  REGISTRAR PROVIDE CERTAIN SERVICES RELATING TO THE CITY’S
  GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION - MARCH 8, 22011

The Issue

Shall the City Council adopt Resolutions R10-20 and R10-21 relating to the City’s General
Municipal Election to be held on March 8, 2011?

Background and Analysis

The City’s General Municipal Election will be held on Tuesday, March 8, 2011. In order to comply
with the Elections Calendar, the process must begin with the adoption of certain resolutions as
follows:

1.  Resolution R10-20 calling for the election of three members of the City Council, and
2.  Resolution R10-21 requesting the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors to have the
  County Registrar/Recorder provide certain election services.

The Elections Code governs the dates of the election calendar. The period Monday, November 15,
2010 through Friday, December 10, 2010 at 5:00 PM is established as the dates for filing of
nomination papers with the City Clerk. If an incumbent fails to file by the December 10th deadline,
the filing period will be extended five days to 5:00 PM on Wednesday, December 15th.

Nomination papers may be taken out and returned during normal city business hours, 8:00 AM to
5:00 PM, Monday through Friday. During the filing period, City Hall will be closed Thursday,
November 24th, and Friday November 25th in observance of Thanksgiving.

The Los Angeles County Registrar/Recorder provides data processing, voter registration
information, consolidation of precincts, verification of signatures and miscellaneous voter services
to the City and our elections consultants, Martin & Chapman. The City must adopt a resolution
requesting that the County provide these services. Costs for the County services during the 2009
municipal election, excluding reimbursement of costs from the City of Los Angeles for
consolidation, totaled $2,017.

Fiscal Impact
CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
OCTOBER 12, 2010
  17
 The City has budgeted $28,800 for services related to conducting the 2011 General Municipal
Election, which includes the services of Martin & Chapman, printing and mailing of a sample ballot
to each registered voter, processing of absentee ballots, County services and Election Day services.
This budget assumes cost sharing with the City of Los Angeles for conducting their consolidated
election for the Community College District Board of Trustees.

The costs associated with the 2009 Municipal Election totaled $39,595, excluding the purchase of a
ballot counter. The net cost to the City, after reimbursement from the City of Los Angeles for
conducting the consolidated election, totaled $22,380 ($1.94/registered voter).

Recommendation

It is recommended that the City Council adopt:

  1. Resolution R10-20 calling for the election of City officers, and

  2. Resolution R10-21 requesting the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors to have
  the County Registrar/Recorder provide certain election services.

The Issue

Shall the City Council agree to a request to consolidate the Primary Nominating Election of the City
of Los Angeles with the City of Palos Verdes Estates’ General Municipal Election to be held on
March 8, 2011 and adopt Resolution R10-22?

Background and Analysis

The City of Los Angeles primary election falls on the same day as other general municipal elections
within Los Angeles County conducted in March of odd-numbered years. The City of Los Angeles
also conducts elections on behalf of the Los Angeles Unified School District and the Los Angeles
Community College District.

Since 2003, the City of Palos Verdes Estates has agreed to a request from the City of Los Angeles
to consolidate the LA Community College District Board election with our municipal election. The
Community College District encompasses 100% of the jurisdictional boundaries of Palos Verdes
Estates and once again, the City of Los Angeles requests that their election, which involves a
nomination election for four members of the Community College District Board of Trustees
(Districts 1, 3, 5 & 7) be consolidated with the City’s March 8, 2011 election. A copy of the
resolution from the City of Los Angeles requesting the consolidation is attached.

The City has not experienced any difficulties in conducting a consolidated election and the City has
reaped significant benefit in that we are able to share costs for conducting the election with the City
of Los Angeles. A consolidated election, in which all candidate names appear on the same ballot, is
also less confusing to voter who otherwise would cast two separate ballots at their same polling
location.

City of Los Angeles election regulations do not permit candidate statements for the Community
College District Board. The only information that will appear in the City’s Sample Ballot, which is
election information mailed to all voters, is the listing of the candidates’ names by district for the
CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
OCTOBER 12, 2010
  19
 Community College election. Thus, it is not likely that Palos Verdes Estates offices would be “lost”
or diminished by information related to the Community College District election.

In the event the City cancels its election due to insufficient candidates, meaning the number of
certified candidates filing equals the number of available offices, the City will notify the City of Los
Angeles, which will then conduct their own election within Palos Verdes Estates for the Community
College District Board.

Alternatives Available to the City Council

1.  Consent to consolidation with the City of Los Angeles for purposes of conducting a
  consolidated election and adopt R10-22.

2.  Decline to agree to the request to consolidate. Under this scenario, the City of Los Angeles
  will run a concurrent election using the same polling locations as the City’s election, but
  with shared poll workers, separate ballots and separate absentee ballot process for all voters
  within the City of Palos Verdes Estates. In addition, the City of Palos Verdes Estates will
  bear the full cost of conducting the municipal election.

Recommendation

It is recommended that the City Council accept the request to consolidate the City of Los Angeles
Primary Nominating Election for the Los Angeles Community College District Board of Trustees
with the City of Palos Verdes Estates General Municipal Election of March 8, 2011 and adopt
Resolution R10-22.

Budget Impact

If the City Council agrees to consolidation, the City of Palos Verdes Estates will be able to charge
the City of Los Angeles for related election costs. The City has budgeted $28,800 to cover the cost
of this election and the budget assumed consolidation with Los Angeles and cost sharing for the
election. As a result of the consolidation in 2009, the City received a reimbursement of $17,215
from the City of Los Angeles and a net election cost of $22,380 to Palos Verdes Estates.

TO:  JOSEPH M. HOEFGEN, CITY MANAGER

FROM:  ALEXA D. DAVIS, ADMINISTRATIVE ANALYST

SUBJECT:  SPECIAL EVENT APPLICATION FOR PALOS VERDES ART CENTER’S
  “HOMES TOUR EXTRAORDINAIRE” AND BOUTIQUE TO BE HELD ON
  APRIL 15-16, 2011

DATE:  OCTOBER 12, 2010

ISSUE

Shall the City approve a Special Event Application for the Palos Verdes Art Center to host its annual
“Homes Tour Extraordinaire” and Boutique on Friday and Saturday, April 15-16, 2011 from 10:00
a.m. – 4:00 p.m.?

BACKGROUND

The Circle, a major support group of the Palos Verdes Art Center, is requesting permission to sponsor a
home tour and boutique highlighting the history of Malaga Cove Plaza. Proceeds will benefit the Palos
Verdes Art Center by supporting the Center’s art education, exhibition and outreach programs. To
date, the Circle has raised over $1 million to support the Art Center and its efforts. The “Homes Tour
Extraordinaire,” held for over twenty years, is a successful fundraiser for the Palos Verdes Art Center
with more than 600 patrons.

The tour is proposed to be held on Friday and Saturday, April 15-16, 2011 and involves four homes
and a boutique sale, all in the City of Palos Verdes Estates. The homes include the following locations:

  2433 Via Campesina (apartment building)
  637 Via Horquilla
  748 Via Somante
  424 Paseo del Mar

Residents within 300’ of the location will be notified that a home tour will be conducted in their
neighborhood. A sample notification letter is attached.

In addition to the homes being toured, the Palos Verdes Art Center is proposing a Boutique Sale as
one stop on the tour. The Boutique Sale has been a component to previous Palos Verdes Art Center
Homes Tours; however, it was always held at the Center located at 5504 W. Crestridge Road in
Rancho Palos Verdes. Due to the anticipated renovation at the Center, this year only, the Art Center

CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
OCTOBER 12, 2010
  21
 is proposing that the Boutique Sale be held on a portion of Olmsted Place in Palos Verdes Estates
(Palos Verdes Drive West / Via Tejon) for both days of the event.

The Boutique Sale would include up to 12 vendors in uniform 10 x 10 spaces with a tent/tents
covering the area. Vendors would be selling upscale items like clothing, crafts, jewelry, etc.
Additionally, as part of the Boutique stop on the tour, lunch is planned to be provided by The
Yellow Vase (a restaurant scheduled to be opened in Malaga Cove Plaza by the event dates). Event
organizers have sought Malaga Cove Plaza business approval and have included letters of support
with their application (see attached).

Additionally, the traditional Palos Verdes Art Center Malaga Cove Lawn Art Shows located on the
green space between the Malaga Cove Plaza parking lot and Palos Verdes Drive West (Malaga Cove
Lawn), would normally fall on the same weekend as this event. For this weekend only, both groups
are interested in the two events coinciding on the same days (Friday and Saturday) in order to
maximize exposure for their respective events. The Art Show will come to Council for consideration
and approval in a separate Special Event Application early next year.

Parking for the Home Tour would be at the First Church of Christian Science at Palos Verdes Drive
North and Via Campesina. A shuttle bus would take participants to the homes and boutique as
described below.

The Special Event Application has been reviewed by all municipal departments. Although the
homes tour portion of the event is a standard and traditional event held within the City, staff has
noted some concerns regarding the use of Olmsted Place for the boutique portion of the tour.

1.  Vehicular Safety –The location at Olmsted Place will likely cause a distraction to motorists
  at an already complex intersection. Staff has concerns about the difficulty to navigate
  through traffic resulting in potential collisions.

  Art Center Response: Event organizers are willing to pay for a Police Officer for the
  duration of the event in order to mitigate traffic impacts.

2.  Pedestrian Safety – This event will increase the amount of pedestrians in and around the
  Plaza area. With Olmsted Place surrounded by streets on three sides, and an entrance to the
  Plaza on the fourth side, many pedestrians, not already a part of the tour, would have to
  cross streets in order to reach the Boutique.

  Art Center Response: Several volunteers will be stationed with safety vests to direct
  pedestrian traffic through designated crosswalks to and from Olmsted Place as necessary.

3.  Parking – The first day of the event is proposed on a business day, thus potentially limiting
  parking for businesses in the Plaza.

  Art Center Response: Boutique customers that are not part of the Homes Tour will be
  directed to observe all parking limitations. Individuals interested in joining the tour will be

CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
OCTOBER 12, 2010
  22
   directed to purchase a ticket and then park at the designated parking lot at the First Church
  of Christian Science.

4.  Setting a Precedent – Olmsted Place has never been used for an event since its dedication on
  February 8, 2000 as a tribute to Frederick Law Olmsted, Jr. Staff has concerns that if the
  City were to allow one event to occur there, it would open the door to future events. The
  City has had a strict policy on what parks can be used for events, thus have limited park use
  to Farnham Martin Park and Lunada Bay Park, and artists on Malaga Cove Lawn.

  Art Center Response: This is a one-time use of Olmsted Place due to the scheduled
  renovation of the Center and event organizers will not make future requests.

Due to the concerns listed above, City staff has reviewed the following alternatives for where/when
the Boutique could be held with less impact.

1.  The use of a portion of the Malaga Cove Lawn to be shared with the Art Show artists on the
  dates proposed.

  Impacts:  Reduced vehicular and pedestrian traffic resulting in safer surroundings.
  However, this option must be coordinated with the artists of the Art Shows.

2.  The use of Farnham Martin Park, adjacent to the Malaga Cove Library, on the dates proposed.

  Impacts:  Farnham Martin Park has a slope in the grassy area that would be difficult to
  set-up equipment. Additionally, there are concerns of suitable catering facilities in order for
  lunch to be served to patrons.

3.  Different dates only on weekend days in order to not impact businesses in the Plaza, as well as
  the use of Malaga Cove Lawn in lieu of Olmsted Place, similar to the Art Shows held on
  Saturdays and Sundays on the Malaga Cove Lawn.

  Impacts:  The “Home Tour Extraordinaire” has historically always fallen on the same
  Friday and Saturday in April. Additionally, the group has experimented in past years with
  hosting the event on a Saturday and Sunday. This resulted in a decrease of volunteers and
  participants of the tour.

All fees have been paid and the Indemnity Agreement has been received. The Certificate of Insurance
will be obtained upon City Council approval of the Special Event Application. The Palos Verdes Art
Center and its Circle group is well aware of the City’s concerns and are willing to abide by and pay for
any conditions set by the City in order to secure approval.

ALTERNATIVES AVAILABLE TO COUNCIL

1.  Council may approve the Special Event Application to conduct the Homes Tour and Boutique
  at Olmsted Place.

CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
OCTOBER 12, 2010
  23
 2.  Council may approve the Special Event Application for the Home Tour with the Boutique Sale
  held at the Malaga Cove Lawn.

3.  Council may choose not to approve the Special Event Application.

4.  Council may impose additional conditions or restrictions on the sponsors of the tour.

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the City Council review the Special Event Application for Palos Verdes Art
Center’s home tour at four residential properties within the City limits and provide direction on the
location of the Art Center’s boutique to be held April 15 and 16, 2011 from 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

SPECIAL EVENT APPLICATION FOR PALOS VERDES ART CENTER’S “HOMES TOUR
EXTRAORDINAIRE” AND BOUTIQUE TO BE HELD APRIL 15 AND 16, 2011

City Manager Hoefgen indicated the Palos Verdes Art Center (PVAC) has conducted its annual homes
tour for over 20 years. This year the theme is “Historic Palos Verdes.” All four homes are located in
PVE and participants will ride shuttle buses to visit the homes. Next year the PVAC building will be
undergoing remodeling and the organizers are unable to hold the shopping boutique portion of the
event at the center. The boutique consists of 12 individual vendors either under one large tent or
individual tents. In the Special Event Application, the PVAC originally proposed that the boutique sale
take place at Olmsted Place from the flagpole toward the Malaga Cove Plaza side. The staff report lists
some of staff’s concerns regarding the use of Olmstead Place. There have been a number of
discussions back and forth with PVAC regarding where to allow the boutique to take place. One of the
alternatives is to have the boutique share the Malaga Cove Plaza lawn with the PVAC regular (Spring
to Fall) monthly art show. The PVAC has agreed to this compromise.

Councilmember Bird asked if the regular PVAC art show dates could be changed for this event. Ann
Willens, Director of PVAC, responded that the art shows have been taking place for over 40 years on
the same weekend and some feel that the homes tour will bring additional customers to the art show
and MC Plaza businesses.

Ann Willens said they conceive of having the artists on one side of the large pine tree and the boutique
will be on the other side. She said she has asked the City to block off the perimeter of the parking lot
so the businesses are not affected by event. Additionally, they have asked the three plaza restaurants
for bids on catering the lunch. She also noted that the homes addresses are not printed on the tickets;
all participants will be shuttled from the First Christ Scientist Church on Via Campesina to the homes
and then to MC Plaza for the boutique and lunch.

Mayor Humphrey thanked Ms. Willens for agreeing to have the two events share the MC Plaza lawn.

Councilmember Bird thanked the PVAC for their willingness to have volunteers directing pedestrian
traffic if necessary. He asked if it was the PVAC’s preference to be in MC Plaza lawn or Olmsted
Place. Ms. Willens said their preference would be Olmsted Place, but they like MC Plaza and
understand the problems with using Olmsted Place. They are willing to pay for a police officer to
direct traffic as well as volunteers in MC Plaza to keep things orderly. She said they have been running
this event for about 25 years so they are well versed in how to do it properly. She also commented that
the Art Center actually started in Malaga Cove Plaza.

Councilmember Perkins wanted to clarify that PVAC was willing to pay for a police officer whether
the boutique was located on Olmsted Place or MC Plaza.

Councilmember Goodhart said he reviewed the staff report and the concerns raised by staff. He has
attended the art shows in MC Plaza and it is usually very crowded already. He wondered if the Palos
Verdes Drive West entrance between MC Plaza and Olmsted Place were blocked off, whether the tents
could be placed there. Mayor Humphrey said this was discussed at the Mayors meeting and she was
not comfortable with that option as there would not be access for emergency vehicles.

Mayor Pro Tem Rea said he had asked staff about using the island area surrounding Neptune Fountain,
but there were concerns with this area being in the middle of a parking lot.

Councilmember Goodhart said that the small portion of street could be blocked and the traffic flow
through the parking lot would not be interrupted. Mayor Humphrey was not in favor of this option due
to concerns with emergency vehicle access being blocked. She was also in favor of placing a police
officer directing traffic.

CITY COUNCIL  3
OCTOBER 12, 2010
 Nancy Bond, co-chair of the PVAC Home Tour and PVE resident, has been looking since summer for
a place to hold the boutique due to the planned remodel of the PVAC. She looked at Farnham Martin
Park and believed it is too much of a slope for the tents. She was in favor of barricading the entry from
PVDW between the MC Plaza and Olmsted Place. She thought this would be the perfect spot for the
shuttle bus to pull in and safely disembark passengers. Councilmember Goodhart and Mayor
Humphrey were still concerned with pedestrian safety. Ms. Bond believed that dropping passengers on
PVDW would decrease the amount of available parking.

Ann Willens said the PVAC would work closely with the City to figure out the best solution for traffic
flow and safety. It would be fitting to have the event in Malaga Cove as next year will be the PVAC
80th anniversary.

Mayor Humphrey asked the City Manager who the PVAC should work with to work out the logistics.
Manager Hoefgen said the point of contact would be Administrative Analyst Alexa Davis.

Councilmember Bird was in favor of allowing the event to take place on Olmsted Place as it is a public
area and PVAC is a very deserving and responsible group. He does not believe there would be enough
room for the dual events using just the MC Plaza lawn. The event will end at 4:00 p.m. each day and
will not impede Friday’s commuter traffic, especially with a traffic officer in place. Secondly, if it
becomes necessary to close a street or two to allow the event, he believes that the police department
has expertise to make that safely happen. He supports approving the Special Event Application and
allowing the boutique to be held on Olmsted Place and, if necessary, overflow on to MC Plaza.

Councilmember Goodhart said his idea of blocking off part of the street was due to his not being
comfortable with Olmsted Place being covered in tents. What he hadn’t thought of was the fact that if
Council allows the PVAC to hold a one-time event on Olmsted Place then another group can come
along and want to hold an event there also. His compromise would be to allow use of Olmsted Place
on the east side of the flagpole only, but then there would be pedestrian traffic going across the street.
Hence, the idea of placing barricades to block off the entrance from PVDW.

Mayor Humphrey said she was willing to leave it to staff to work out the best plan for safety.

Councilmember Perkins said her idea was closer to Councilmember Goodhart’s position. She did not
like the idea of using Olmsted Place due to safety concerns with pedestrians and traffic. She did like
the idea of keeping the boutique on the northeast side of the flagpole only if there is no safety issue
with closing the street access. With a large number of people there will need to be access for
emergency vehicles – she would defer to staff for protocol for street closures. She thought it may be
safer to block the entrance from PVDW. Nancy Bond said that was the PVAC’s initial thought also.
Councilmember Perkins would be in support of Councilmember Goodhart’s proposal as long as there
are no safety issues. If the street must stay open she would not support the use of Olmsted Place.

Mayor Humphrey said the City has been approached by other groups to use Olmsted Place and it has
been declined since it is a designated memorial.

Mayor Pro Tem Rea said he had also been concerned about using Olmsted Place due to the same
concerns of the other Council members. He said his compromise was a suggestion to use the island
around Neptune Fountain, but this area is in the middle of the parking lot with cars moving all around
it. He was happy to hear that the PVAC agreed to share MC Plaza area.

Councilmember Goodhart said he is worried that an additional 10 or so tents on MC Plaza would make
it too crowded.

Mayor Humphrey asked the PVAC if the Art Show could be held on another weekend, but it has been
a long standing event and they do not want to change the dates and think that the boutique will bring
additional customers.

Councilmember Goodhart believes that having the 10 tents on the east side of the Olmsted Place
flagpole along with barricades on the PVDW entrance would relieve some of the pedestrian congestion
on the MC Plaza lawn.

CITY COUNCIL  4
OCTOBER 12, 2010
 Councilmember Perkins said it is not the Council’s role to micro-manage the exact solution. She
wondered if the PVAC could have a reduced number of artists at this event on Friday, and the full
number on Saturday. Ann Willens said they will probably have to limit the number of artists who
participate.

Councilmember Bird said he was in favor of the compromise that Councilmember Goodhart suggested
to use the area northeast of the flagpole on Olmsted Place. He asked Chief Dreiling if the Council did
authorize the use of this area of Olmsted Place and close the entrance to PVDW to accommodate
traffic, the placing of tents and the shuttle stop - would there be any issue impeding public safety or
emergency vehicles. Chief Dreiling said if the Council proposes to place tents on the east side of
Olmsted Place, closing the access road from PVDW would be essential. He believes it could be done,
but he would have to sit down with the Public Works Director and staff and work out how it could
work. It has been done in the past. Councilmember Bird asked if there were any emergencies at any
location that closing the access road would make it impossible for emergency vehicles to respond to.
Chief Dreiling would like to place barricades only and not tents on the street in order to make it safer
and easier for vehicle access.

Mayor Humphrey said she feels the Council has no objection to the use of MC Plaza and, if deemed
safe, the use of a portion of Olmsted Place and a portion of the street.

It was moved by Councilmember Goodhart, seconded by Councilmember Bird, and unanimously
approved by a roll call vote to approve the Special Event Application for the Palos Verdes Art Center
home tour at four residential properties within the City limits and, if deemed to be safe by the Police
Chief, the northeast portion of Olmsted Place with provisions for barricading for public safety for the
Art Center’s vendor boutique Friday and Saturday, April 15 and 16, 2011 from 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
